segs.text: What if your A.I. remembered what you told it three months ago?
parts: What if your A.I. remembered what you told it three months ago?

segs.text: On Monday, Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier A.I. model, along with a bigger version, called Muse Wonder Full.
parts: On Monday, Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier A.I. model,
along with a bigger version, called Muse Wonder Full.

segs.text: The headline feature is what Meta calls active memory: holding on to what matters to you, over days, weeks and months.
parts: The headline feature is what Meta calls active memory:
holding on to what matters to you, over days, weeks and months.

segs.text: That's the missing piece for A.I. agents. An assistant that forgets everything is stuck on small tasks. One that remembers can take on long-running work.
parts: That's the missing piece for A.I. agents.
An assistant that forgets everything is stuck on small tasks.
One that remembers can take on long-running work.

segs.text: Wonder is open to developers through Meta's paid API. Wonder Full is limited to subscribers of its coding tool.
parts: Wonder is open to developers through Meta's paid API.
Wonder Full is limited to subscribers of its coding tool.

segs.text: The catch: the benchmark scores come from Meta's own testing. And a model that remembers you raises a bigger question: who controls that memory?
parts: The catch: the benchmark scores come from Meta's own testing.
And a model that remembers you raises a bigger question: who controls that memory?

segs.text: Memory makes agents useful. Who owns that memory will decide whether they're trusted.
parts: Who owns that memory will decide whether they're trusted.

segs.text: Three months from now, it might remember. Make sure you can choose what it keeps.
parts: Three months from now, it might remember.
Make sure you can choose what it keeps.
